analyst.summary: Bosch Ltd's FY26 print (revenue Rs 20,035 cr +10.8%, PAT Rs 2,773 cr +37.6%) confirms a pristine, debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.008x, interest coverage 98x) and real, funded strategic moves to de-risk the ICE-to-EV transition -- a Tata AutoComp e-axle/motor JV for direct EV participation and a Rs 9,068 cr acquisition of Bosch's own group ABS/ESC/airbag business (RBIC) for powertrain-agnostic content -- layered on a near-term ICE-content tailwind from OBD-II emission norms (Two-Wheeler sales +69% in FY26). But the quant Quality score (31st percentile) is earned: operating margin has been structurally stuck at 12-13% since FY21 (versus 18-19% pre-Covid) and over 60% of FY26's headline PAT growth traces to a lumpy jump in non-core other/treasury income rather than operations -- a margin and capital-efficiency story, not a leverage one. At ~44x trailing earnings and ~8x book for a ~10-11% grower, valuation is full and not underwritten by independent sell-side (JM Financial, ICICI Securities both target at/below CMP). Net: Hold -- no fundamental red flag justifies selling a debt-free, actively de-risking compounder, but nothing here is cheap enough to add to either.
